# dsm_package (Resource)

Installs and controls a package from Synology DSM Package Center. Existing packages are adopted automatically. Package removal is disabled by default because uninstalling an application can also remove its configuration and data.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dsm_package" "container_manager" {
  name    = "ContainerManager"
  volume  = "/volume1"
  running = true

  # Keep the package installed if the Terraform resource is removed.
  uninstall_on_destroy = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Package Center identifier, for example `ContainerManager` or `FileStation`.

### Optional

- `running` (Boolean) Whether the package should be running. Changes start or stop the installed package in place.
- `uninstall_on_destroy` (Boolean) Permanently uninstall the package when this resource is destroyed. Defaults to `false`; destroy then only removes the package from Terraform state. Enable with care because DSM packages may remove configuration or application data.
- `volume` (String) Volume path used for a new installation, for example `/volume1`. DSM does not expose the installed volume through this API.

### Read-Only

- `can_uninstall` (Boolean) Whether DSM allows this package to be uninstalled. System packages usually report `false`.
- `description` (String) Package description reported by DSM.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable package name reported by DSM.
- `id` (String) Package identifier used by DSM Package Center.
- `maintainer` (String) Package maintainer reported by DSM.
- `status` (String) Raw lifecycle status reported by DSM, such as `running`, `stop`, or `broken`.
- `version` (String) Installed package version.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import dsm_package.container_manager ContainerManager
```
